title: TEXT OF THE OBSERVATION MADE BY THE HON'BLE CHAIRMAN, RAJYA SABHA REGARDING DISCOURTEOUS AND UNDIGNIFIED COMMENTS BEING MADE BY MEMBERS INTERRUPTING THE SPEECH OF OTHER MEMBERS IN THE HOUSE
body_text:
CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, certain instances have come to my notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by Members interrupting the speech of other Members in the House. I would advise that Hon'ble Members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow Members.  Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues.
****
RKK

enrichment.summary: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha issued an observation cautioning Members of Parliament against making discourteous and undignified comments while interrupting other Members' speeches in the House. He urged MPs to avoid hurting the sentiments of fellow Members and to respect India's diverse regional cultures and identities.
enrichment.context:
Parliamentary decorum and the conduct of proceedings in the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha are governed by rules of procedure and conventions that empower the presiding officer (Chairman in Rajya Sabha, Speaker in Lok Sabha) to maintain order and dignity in the House. Instances of unparliamentary remarks, personal attacks, or disrespect toward regional or cultural identities of members have periodically drawn attention, prompting presiding officers to issue advisories or expunge remarks from records. Such observations reflect the broader concern about eroding decorum in legislative debates and the presiding officer's role as custodian of House discipline under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business.

India's diversity—linguistic, regional, and cultural—is a recurring theme invoked in parliamentary conduct, given Articles 15 and 29 of the Constitution which safeguard against discrimination and protect cultural and educational rights of minorities and regions. This observation, while not a policy announcement, underscores the functioning of parliamentary institutions and the presiding officer's disciplinary and moral authority, which is relevant for understanding India's legislative processes and parliamentary ethics.

prelims_questions.question: Who among the following presides over the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha and has the authority to maintain order and decorum in the House?
options: The Vice-President of India as ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha only
prelims_questions.explanation: The Vice-President of India serves as the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64 of the Constitution and presides over its proceedings, maintaining order and decorum.

prelims_questions.question: Under which provision of the Constitution does the Vice-President of India act as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
prelims_questions.explanation: Article 64 of the Constitution states that the Vice-President of India shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
